blindSummary: This state/province is grouped in the framework dossier together with its neighbouring jurisdiction under the heading "the border-region courts' non-recognition of trans women as women", reflecting their shared judicial geography. However, the specific court-of-appeals annulment underlying that grouping was delivered in the neighbouring jurisdiction, and this region's own data contribution is limited to a 0.84 % share of national cases (2024) — among the lowest in the country, in a year that saw increases in 11 of 16 regions. No trans-specific incident, court ruling, or enforcement failure originating here was identified. The grouping rests on the shared judicial-climate framing and the broader pattern — reported in both the 2024 and 2025 annual surveys of the national LGBTQ+ rights organisation — that homo/transphobia cases rose in most regions outside the capital region. Nothing recorded here materially changes the framework described above; the file notes the absence of any positive institutional finding (no diversity office, no municipal ordinance, no documented court protection).
blindSourceSummaries: A national television crime report: a regional court of appeals in the neighbouring jurisdiction annulled the entire trial over the killing of a transgender woman after holding that the country's "femicide" offence protects only "a person biologically female", so the conviction could not stand as framed — a finding that the country's strongest gendered-violence protection does not extend to trans women. The framework dossier cites it as the basis for grouping both transborder jurisdictions on shared judicial geography; the ruling itself belongs to the neighbour.

The national LGBTQ+ rights organisation's 23rd annual human-rights report on sexual and gender diversity (2024 data, published March 2025), full per-region table: 2,847 recorded cases nationally (+78.7 %), with this state/province holding a 0.84 % share — among the lowest in the country — in a year that saw increases in 11 of 16 regions; small-share regions where a single case dominates the rate.
